output.answer: As of November 11, 2026, Johnson & Johnson's most recent completed acquisition is Firefly Bio, Inc., closed July 29, 2026 for $1 billion in cash to add its Firelink degrader antibody conjugate (DAC) oncology platform. That followed the $3.05 billion acquisition of Halda Therapeutics (completed December 29, 2025) and the roughly $14.6 billion purchase of Intra-Cellular Therapies (completed April 2, 2025), maker of CAPLYTA, which anchors J&J's neuroscience push. In 2024, J&J acquired Shockwave Medical for about $13.1 billion, Ambrx Biopharma for about $2.0 billion in equity value, Proteologix for $850 million, and V-Wave for $600 million upfront plus up to roughly $1.1 billion in milestones — after its approximately $16.6 billion acquisition of Abiomed announced in November 2022. Separately, on July 29, 2026, J&J struck a collaboration with Flagship-founded Sail Biomedicines with an exclusive option to acquire the company for an additional $2.58 billion, so that deal is an option, not a completed acquisition.
caveats: Deal values for Shockwave ($13.1B), Ambrx (~$2.0B), Proteologix ($850M), V-Wave ($600M upfront) and Abiomed (~$16.6B) are taken from the announcement press releases; those pages state the announced transaction value, not a later closing confirmation.

The Sail Biomedicines arrangement is a collaboration/licensing deal with an exclusive option to acquire (an additional $2.58 billion upon exercise), not a completed acquisition; it is shown as 'Pending' in deal trackers.
The list covers J&J's major acquisitions from 2022 through 2026; it is not an exhaustive record of the company's full M&A history (J&J has made dozens of smaller deals over its ~140-year history).

passages.quote: **NEW BRUNSWICK, NJ (July 29, 2026)** – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of Firefly Bio, Inc., a biotechnology company advancing its proprietary Firelink™ degrader antibody conjugate (DAC) platform, for $1 billion in cash. The Firelink™ DAC platform expands Johnson & Johnson’s oncology portfolio and advances its ambition to develop targeted therapies for some of the most prevalent and difficult-to-treat solid tumors, including KRAS-driven cancers, where patients continue to face significant unmet need\[1\].

**NEW BRUNSWICK, NJ (December 29, 2025)** – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) (the “Company”) today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of Halda Therapeutics OpCo, Inc. (“Halda”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company with a proprietary Regulated Induced Proximity TArgeting Chimera (RIPTAC™) platform to develop oral, targeted therapies for multiple types of solid tumors, including prostate cancer, for $3.05 billion in cash.

**New Brunswick, N.J., April 2, 2025** – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced it has completed its acquisition of Intra-Cellular Therapies, Inc. Intra-Cellular Therapies is now part of Johnson & Johnson and will operate as a business unit within Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine.

**NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J. and SANTA CLARA, Calif., April 5, 2024 –** Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) and Shockwave Medical, Inc. (Nasdaq: SWAV) (“Shockwave”) today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement under which Johnson & Johnson will acquire all outstanding shares of Shockwave for $335.00 per share in cash, corresponding to an enterprise value of approximately $13.1 billion including cash acquired. The transaction was approved by both companies’ boards of directors.

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J.— August 20, 2024 – Johnson & Johnson1 (NYSE: JNJ) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire V-Wave Ltd., a privately-held company focused on developing innovative treatment options for patients with heart failure. Under the terms of the agreement, Johnson & Johnson will acquire V-Wave for an upfront payment of $600 million, subject to customary adjustments, with the potential for additional regulatory and commercial milestone payments up to approximately $1.1 billion. V-Wave will join Johnson & Johnson as part of Johnson & Johnson MedTech.

**NEW BRUNSWICK, NJ (January 8, 2024)** – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) announced today it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Ambrx Biopharma, Inc., or Ambrx (NASDAQ: AMAM), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with a proprietary synthetic biology technology platform to design and develop next-generation antibody drug conjugates (ADCs), in an all-cash merger transaction for a total equity value of approximately $2.0 billion, or $1.9 billion net of estimated cash acquired.

**NEW BRUNSWICK, NJ (May 16, 2024)** – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) announced today that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Proteologix, Inc., a privately-held biotechnology company focused on bispecific antibodies for immune-mediated diseases, for $850 million in cash, with potential for an additional milestone payment.

**New Brunswick, N.J. and Danvers, Mass.**, **November 1, 2022** – Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ), the world’s largest, most diversified healthcare products company, and Abiomed (NASDAQ: ABMD), a world leader in breakthrough heart, lung and kidney support technologies, today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement under which Johnson & Johnson will acquire through a tender offer all outstanding shares of Abiomed, for an upfront payment of $380.00 per share in cash, corresponding to an enterprise value of approximately $16.6 billion which includes cash acquired. Abiomed shareholders will also receive a non-tradeable contingent value right (CVR) entitling the holder to receive up to $35.00 per share in cash if certain commercial and clinical milestones are achieved. The transaction was unanimously approved by both companies’ boards of directors.

Johnson & Johnson has completed its [$14.6 billion acquisition](https://njbiz.com/johnson-johnson-to-buy-bedminster-based-drugmaker-for-14-6b/) of Bedminster-based neurological drugmaker Intra-Cellular Therapies.

Johnson & Johnson entered strategic agreements with Sail Biomedicines to develop in vivo CAR-T therapies for immune-mediated diseases, with an exclusive option to acquire Sail. J&J makes total initial payments of $785 million, including a $465 million equity investment, plus $140 million in contingent development milestone payments; exercising the acquisition option would trigger an additional $2.58 billion payment. Sail's platform is designed to generate CAR-T cells directly in the body, avoiding ex vivo cell manufacturing. J&J guided to adjusted EPS dilution of roughly $0.18 in 2026 and $1.28 in 2027 assuming option exercise.

Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire V-Wave Ltd., a heart-failure device company, for $600 million upfront with potential additional milestone payments up to approximately $1.1 billion; V-Wave joined J&J MedTech.

Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire Proteologix, Inc., a bispecific-antibody biotech focused on immune-mediated diseases including atopic dermatitis, for $850 million in cash plus a potential milestone payment.
Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire Shockwave Medical for $335.00 per share in cash, an enterprise value of approximately $13.1 billion including cash acquired.
Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire Ambrx Biopharma, a clinical-stage antibody-drug-conjugate (ADC) biotech, for a total equity value of approximately $2.0 billion ($28.00 per share in cash).

Johnson & Johnson agreed to acquire Abiomed for $380.00 per share upfront (enterprise value approximately $16.6 billion) plus a non-tradeable CVR of up to $35.00 per share; Abiomed operates as a standalone business within J&J MedTech.

Johnson & Johnson entered a strategic collaboration with Flagship-founded Sail Biomedicines to develop in vivo CAR-T therapies, with $785 million in initial payments (including a $465 million equity investment) and an exclusive option to acquire Sail for an additional $2.58 billion — pending, not completed.
